extracted.intended_audience: CIA directorates and agency managers responsible for preparing OMB Circular A-44 (Management Review and Improvement Program) reports
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit an agency (directorate-level) contribution to the OMB Circular A-44 Management Review and Improvement Program report, following prescribed sections, format, responsibilities, and deadlines. Emphasis is on identifying and achieving measurable management, productivity, and cost-reduction improvements rather than producing an impressive-looking report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program objective — intensify management review to increase performance at lower cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The President instructed each Department and Agency to intensify management review of federal activities, programs and services with the explicit goal of substantially increasing the performance level, productivity and quality of federal programs at lower cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency support should be positive and constructive; the objective is to improve program management, productivity, evaluation and performance which will benefit the Agency and the government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of reports — focus on identification and achievement of improvement goals
rubrics_metrics.description: While obviously we must prepare the required reports, it should be kept in mind that the objective is not the preparation of an impressive report. Rather it is the identification and achievement of goals and objectives in improvement in program management, productivity, evaluation and performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should document real improvements and planned actions, not merely produce paperwork. Emphasize measurable results and follow-through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow OMB Circular A-44 prescribed format
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide a common basis for preparation of an overall Agency report, it is essential that each Section be prepared in accordance with the format prescribed by OMB. Self-designed forms or formats will have to be returned by the Office of Planning, Programming, and Budgeting for resubmission in accordance with OMB instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not invent your own format; using the exact OMB structure ensures integration and acceptance. Expect resubmission if noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit details of plans and accomplishments for specified sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Directorate is requested to submit details of plans and accomplishments as outlined in Sections II, IV, V, III, VII and VIII of the attachment (with responsibility assignments noted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare contributions matching the content expectations of those Sections in the attachment; coordinate with assigned coordinators for each Section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned responsibilities for sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspector General will be responsible for Section I. Section III will be prepared by the Director of Finance. Section VIII should be submitted through the Director of Personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these role assignments when preparing or routing material; the Director of Planning, Programming, and Budgeting will integrate all contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination/support for specific sections
rubrics_metrics.description: In carrying out integration, the Director of Planning, Programming, and Budgeting will utilize the advice and guidance of the Special Assistant to the Executive Director-Comptroller for Information Control with respect to Section V; the support of the IP Board for Section IV; and the Director of Personnel with regard to Section VII.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek and incorporate guidance from these offices when preparing the related Sections to ensure consistency and to take advantage of subject-matter support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Sections I, II and VI to focus on management procedure improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections I, II and VI of this year's report [are] vehicles to focus attention on real improvements in our management procedures for establishing priorities, evaluating performance and setting goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame content in these Sections around concrete changes to procedures that improve priority-setting, performance evaluation, and goal-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure accomplishments against prior Management Effectiveness and Cost Reduction Goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Management Effectiveness and Cost Reduction Goals outlined in last year's report to OMB, Sections III and IV, against which our actual accomplishments should be measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use last year's stated goals (Sections III & IV of prior report) as baseline metrics to assess current accomplishments and to demonstrate progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report only reasonably significant accomplishments and plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Report only those accomplishments and plans which are reasonably significant in terms of their impact on the achievement of some Agency management, operational, or cost reduction goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude trivial items; emphasize items with demonstrable impact. Significance should be defensible under scrutiny and linked to agency goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accomplishments must bear up under scrutiny; plans must reflect serious intentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported accomplishments, of course, should bear up under scrutiny and future management improvement actions and plans should reflect serious intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include evidence and realistic timelines/resources so reported items are credible and executable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and validity over quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality and validity of reported items are more important than quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a few well-documented, impactful items over many superficial entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest priority agency‑wide improvement projects in a covering memorandum
rubrics_metrics.description: In a covering memorandum any contributor may suggest priority improvement projects which require Agency-wide attention and action by the Executive Director-Comptroller in order to implement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you identify projects needing central coordination or resources, propose them explicitly in a covering memo for Executive Director-Comptroller action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and submission routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Directorate is requested to submit to the Director of Planning, Programming, and Budgeting by 15 August 1972 details of plans and accomplishments. The Director of Planning, Programming, and Budgeting is assigned the task of integrating these contributions into an overall agency report which is due at OMB by 1 September.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet the internal 15 August deadline to allow integration; final integrated report must reach OMB by 1 September. Route Section VIII through Director of Personnel as noted.
